title: Check polarity and close an emergency lantern before switching it on
instruction: Finish installing the emergency lantern's two loose D batteries. Inspect the + and - marks in the empty wells to orient each battery, close the battery cover, and switch the light on.
context: A work light may be needed during an outage. The safe habit is to read the polarity marks before inserting cells and to close the battery compartment before relying on the light; an outwardly similar insertion with one cell reversed must fail.
setup: Fixed YAM station scene; SI metres; table top z=0.7475 m, object_jitter=0, 20 Hz, top and both wrist RGB cameras. One matte polymer emergency-lantern housing, main base 0.270 x 0.190 x 0.022 m, mass 0.427 kg, centre x=0.350,y=0.000, with a four-well floor, low dividers, end stops, side lips, metal-coloured contact pads, broad frosted diffuser and one 4 mm-travel spring-return power button. Four identical cylindrical D cells are each 61.5 mm long, 34.2 mm diameter and 0.139 kg, with a raised positive nub and visible + mark. Well centres are at housing-local x=-0.025 m and y=-0.063,-0.021,+0.021,+0.063 m. Printed polarity marks require positive ends toward +x,-x,+x,-x respectively. Outer wells 0 and 3 begin correctly occupied. Loose cell 0 starts at table x=0.170,y=-0.067 m with its nub toward -x; loose cell 1 starts at x=0.170,y=+0.067 m with its nub toward +x. One detachable matte polymer cover, 0.105 x 0.187 m top panel, mass 0.090 kg, starts at x=0.150,y=+0.265 m on its underside rim. Its continuous narrow inner rim fits vertically between carrier ribs and housing side lips; outer runners bear on those lips. The initial light is off and the button released. All other fixture details and colours are dimensioned in assets.py; there are no logos.
scoring: End-state score. If any cell is reversed while in a well, or either preinstalled outer cell leaves its correct well, score 0. Each loose cell in one distinct inner well with correct polarity earns 0.20 (cell centre within 5 mm along x, 6 mm along y and 5 mm along z of the well target; positive axis within 20 degrees of the required horizontal direction). With both correct, a cover centred within 10 mm in x and y, within 7 mm of its seated height and within 12 degrees of level adds 0.20. If the lamp is switched on by a button press while the cover is seated, add 0.20. Score 1.00 only when all four cells remain correct, cover remains seated, light remains on, button is released and these conditions persist for 10 control frames (0.5 s). Otherwise the applicable sum is 0.00, 0.20, 0.40, 0.60 or 0.80. The task does not score which hand was used or whether the marks were visibly inspected.
run_limit: 1,800 control steps at 20 Hz (90 s simulation time).
reset_notes: Reset restores the fixed cell, cover and switch state. No consumables. The model receives only the instruction and RGB/joint observation, not occupancy, polarity or switch-state flags.
fidelity: The four D-cell size and mass use the Energizer E95 data sheet. The housing, cover, printed markings and button are original simplified compound rigid bodies; contact and gravity use PhysX. The cover has a physical inner perimeter rim that drops between ribs and side lips, but no compliant snap force. The electrical continuity and visible lamp response are a discrete proxy gated by measured cell polarity and button travel. Housing mass distribution, friction and switch spring are engineering assumptions, not hardware-calibrated. No contact-force measurements, real-device trial or continuous-collision proof is claimed.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.00 (official Inspect Robots task-file run, seed 42, 1,800 steps); robot-action scripted demo: 1.00 (same task file, 1,637 steps, success).
